# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 67 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 67 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_067_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 5 — Why the Righteous Also Suffer

**67:1** "Why, lord," I said, "do some servants of God live uprightly and commit no sin, yet receive so many torments and adversities in their life?" "How long," he said, "will you persist in your lack of understanding? You inquire about everything, always asking questions. You are too persistent in your questioning."

**67:2** "Listen," he said. "Those who seem always to do good and not to sin — do not suppose that they are without sin. They sin each day, though their sins are small: in word, in deed, even in thought. And because their sins are small, the Lord does not punish them greatly, but torments them with lighter afflictions."

**67:3** "But those who have great and accumulated sins receive greater torments, for they are delivered to the angel of punishment for a long time." "Nevertheless, lord," I asked, "even those who have sinned greatly and are being punished — will they eventually be saved?" "Yes," he replied, "but their salvation will be long delayed."

**67:4** I said to him: "Lord, I wish to understand the various kinds of torments and afflictions. Are they of different types?" "Yes," he said. "And I will explain which types apply to which persons."

**67:5** "The torments and afflictions that come upon people in this life are these: losses, and wanderings, and various illnesses, and disturbances of every kind, and separation from friends and loved ones, and poverty, and all manner of trouble. For these are the torments that the servants of God must endure in their lives. For the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them so that they may be purified."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the taxonomy of afflictions in Similitude 6.*
